title: Carrots At Their Carrotiest (and Easiest)
description:
Recipe from Bee Wilson, Adapted by Eric Kim: It doesn’t seem that butter, water and salt should result in carrots that taste this supremely of carrots, but the magic is evident in the incredible distilled carrot flavor, thanks to a little technique.
In the 5 minutes it takes for the water to come to a simmer in a closed pot, the water gains the sweet, root-vegetable flavor of the carrots while also emulsifying with the butter into a glossy sauce. Stemming from the technique beurre fondu, these are buttered carrots, but poached in their own glossy orange liqueur, making them the carrotiest carrots you’ll ever taste.
This recipe comes from the French chef Raymond Blanc, by way of the food writer Bee Wilson, as featured in her 2023 cookbook “The Secret of Cooking.” Her promise is simple but life-changing: “On lifting the lid, you will see that the butter and water have formed a silky emulsion and, because of the quick cooking time, the carrots retain their orange color and sweet flavor in their buttery bath.”
A quickly boiling in a closed, pressurized environment with water, butter and salt is “a great little secret for cooking vegetables; one that has served me well for many years.” Use this technique for mushrooms, green beans, Brussel sprouts, broccoli, and cauliflower.
ingredients: 9 ounces carrots, peeled, trimmed and cut into ½-inch coins (2 to 4 medium)
directions: In a small saucepan or skillet with a lid, combine the carrots, butter, ¼ cup water and a fat pinch of salt.
Put the lid on the pot and place over pretty high (though not boiling high) heat.
Simmer vigorously until the carrots are tender, and the water and butter have reduced and become glossy, 5 to 8 minutes.
Add a tablespoon or two of water if the pan begins to dry out.
